subject: Catalyst Health - Trial acceptance criteria and measurement plan

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Catalyst Health - Trial acceptance criteria and measurement plan

Hi Aisha / Tom —

Thanks again for a productive demo this morning. Per our call, I wanted to capture a concise POC/trial plan so we’re aligned on what success looks like and who owns each piece. I’ve attached a one-page POC plan and a latency/throughput matrix for the test workload we discussed.

Summary / proposed acceptance criteria (high level):
- Latency: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 420ms for 512 token prompts under steady-state.
- Throughput: sustain 45 QPS for 8k-token aggregate traffic during peak test window.
- Cost: target cost <= $0.65 per 1k input+output tokens in the trial configuration (includes batching/quantization).
- Quality: automated match-rate >= 88% on your 120-case prompt set (we’ll use the shared prompt bank); human rating avg >= 4.2/5 on information accuracy for 30 sampled responses. Hallucination rate < 4%.

Evaluation plan & ownership:
- Redwood (Vivek): baseline perf runs, configured batching and cache, provide perf reports and token-cost simulation. (Deliverable: perf report, week 1)
- Catalyst (Aisha/Tom): provide canonical prompt set (120 cases) + 30 human-eval cases and sample production traffic profile. (Deliverable: prompt bank + traffic sample, by Wed 5/20)
- Redwood (Marcus CS): integrate API keys, set up observability dashboard, collect logs/metrics and run quality eval harness. (Deliverable: shared dashboard + eval results, week 2)

Proposed timeline:
- Tue 5/19: finalize prompt bank (Catalyst) and confirm test windows.
- Wed 5/20: Redwood runs baseline perf with default config; initial cost sim sent same day.
- Thu-Fri 5/21-5/22: Quality evaluation (automated + human rating on 30 samples).
- Mon 5/25: Joint review meeting to go over results and decide production next steps.

Next steps for today: please confirm the prompt bank deliverable date and whether procurement needs a separate statement of work for the dedicated trial capacity.

Attachments: Catalyst_POC_plan_v1.pdf (POC scope & step-by-step), latency_throughput_matrix.xlsx (test matrix).

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor

Thanks Neha — this is great and matches our internal expectations. A few quick clarifications:

1) For quality, we want the human rating rubric you used to be shared (can you include the exact questions/scale so our clinical reviewers align?).
2) Procurement asked whether the trial will generate any ePHI and whether Redwood will sign our standard DPA for the test period. I’ve looped procurement on the thread.

We’ll aim to deliver the 120-case prompt bank and the 30-sample human-eval batch by Wednesday 5/20 EOD.

On the timeline: the Mon 5/25 review works for Tom and me — can we do a 10–11am PT slot? Also, Vivek, can you confirm whether the baseline perf runs require any special dataset redaction or if a synthetic traffic profile is fine for the first pass?

Best,

> 2) Procurement asked whether the trial will generate any ePHI and whether Redwood will sign our standard DPA for the test period. I’ve looped procurement on the thread.

Thanks both — quick answers:
- I’ll attach the human-eval rubric (short checklist + 1–5 Likert questions) and the script we use for blind rating. That will be in the shared Drive link.
- For perf runs, synthetic traffic is preferred for the first pass (no real patient data). If you want to run with a redacted sample, we’ll need confirmation of redaction rules — otherwise we will fully avoid ePHI in the trial.
- On DPA: Redwood is happy to sign a limited-scope DPA for trial usage; Marcus will coordinate legal/CD.

Action items I’ll take on: run baseline perf with our 3 default configs (baseline, high-batch, quantized) on Wed 5/20 morning and share the perf table by EOD. I’ll use the latency_throughput_matrix.xlsx you received.
